TITLE: France spared Moody's ratings downgrade as it struggles with unrest
CONTENT: Moody's concluded a periodic review and kept France's credit rating at Aa3 with a negative outlook, easing pressure on the government. The article says bond markets had priced in a downgrade. The French finance ministry attributed the unchanged rating to the credibility of the 2027 finance bill and its plan to keep public finances on a recovery path. It describes challenges passing the bill in parliament and notes that opposition parties could reject it and potentially topple the government. Moody's said the Aa3 rating assumes adoption of a deficit-reducing 2027 budget and that financing costs and social tensions will ease. The article also discusses borrowing costs, investor concerns about the budget deficit and upcoming elections, and the impact of protests and riots on political and fiscal efforts. It adds that Moody's previously identified parliamentary fragmentation as key to its next rating move and mentions the status of savings measures and proposed deficit targets in the 2027 budget.

TITLE: Stocks fall, but tech shares steady after selloff; oil hits highest in nearly six months
CONTENT: Major stock indexes ended lower on Friday while tech shares mostly steadied. The Nasdaq eased and European shares also ended lower. A semiconductors index rose 0.4%. The S&P 500 technology index was also up 0.4%. The S&P 500 energy sector rose 2.5% to a record high. Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel, and US West Texas Intermediate crude closed at $103.27 a barrel. US Treasury yields rose after the 10-year yield posted its biggest one-day drop in nearly four years. Investors focused on earnings season, including upcoming quarterly results from Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. Meta shares ended down 1%; Microsoft was up 0.7%; Alphabet and Amazon eased. American Express shares fell 3.7% and telecom shares including Verizon dropped after a report about SpaceX discussions involving cellular infrastructure companies.

TITLE: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
CONTENT: US stock investors face a pivotal week as corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting pose tests for a market rally. Weakness in technology shares has left investors concerned about the AI trade. The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss, after a tech-heavy drop the prior day, and investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon are set to headline a busy week of quarterly results. The Fed’s interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday could rattle markets. The article also notes attention on US midterm elections on November 3 and discusses expectations for S&P 500 earnings growth based on LSEG IBES data, with earnings viewed as a determinant of whether a tech pullback is a buying opportunity or signals a deeper correction.

TITLE: Exclusive: Meta acquires AI data platform Sundial
CONTENT: Meta has acquired Sundial, an AI-powered data analytics platform. The platform was founded by two former Meta employees, and a spokesperson confirmed the acquisition to Axios. Sundial will be folded into Meta’s new data analytics organization. Sundial co-founders Julie Zhuo and Chandra Narayanan will join Meta. Other Sundial employees, including Meta alumni, will also join, and Sundial will stop serving external customers when the deal closes. The Sundial platform allows businesses to get quick access to reliable data analysis, turning natural-language questions and complex data into simpler, actionable insights via a chatbot plugin. The article also mentions that Meta named Alex Schultz as its first-ever chief data officer in July, and that he leads a Data Analytics Tooling & Agents unit (DATA) responsible for descriptive analysis, experimentation, monitoring critical AI systems, and issuing alerts.

TITLE: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
CONTENT: Wall Street’s main indexes closed lower on Friday. Technology shares steadied somewhat to end a turbulent week tied to the AI trade, with investors looking ahead to corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting. The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss after its biggest one-day drop since June, with concerns about financing costs for heavy AI investment. The S&P 500 technology sector gained, while most S&P 500 sectors fell, including consumer staples, consumer discretionary, and financials. Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies are set to report quarterly results, including Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon, with their AI-related capital spending forecasts expected to be closely watched. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell, as did the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite. For the week, the S&P 500 fell and the Nasdaq dropped, while the Dow rose for a third straight weekly gain. Telecommunications stocks fell after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier; AT&T and T-Mobile declined while Verizon fell and related cell tower operators rose. The energy sector rose to a record high, with Brent crude reaching its highest level since late April after Houthi attacks raised concerns about potential disruptions. American Express fell after raising its profit forecast and announcing plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce. SLB shares rose after beating Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit. University of Michigan data showed U.S. consumer sentiment edged down near a record low in October.

TITLE: ‘Window of vulnerability’: Banks move to restrict AI agent access
CONTENT: The article says multiple banks, including Citi Bank, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and JPMorgan Chase, have taken steps to limit third-party AI agents from accessing their platforms and services. It notes the concern that AI agents could take unwanted actions on behalf of users and cites a 2026 Palo Alto Networks study about agentic AI being a leading cybersecurity risk. A Citi spokesperson is quoted saying third-party AI agents or assistants are not permitted to log into a customer’s account or transact directly within Citi’s digital banking platforms, while customers may authorize agents to limited, read-only access to account information with certain Citi-approved open banking providers. The article also includes a quote about a “window of vulnerability” as AI is weaponized, and it describes consumer concern cited from a Ping report about AI agents misrepresenting personality or values. It further states that Bank of America, Capital One, and other global banks created a coalition in September to warn about agentic technology moving faster than protections, highlighting risks related to AI shopping agents and emphasizing the need for human involvement before payments.

TITLE: Consumer sentiment dips on worries about affordability: UMichigan survey
CONTENT:
The article says consumer sentiment inched down this month, with worries that persistent inflation will weaken buying power. It reports that household perceptions of conditions for purchasing durable goods slumped 18% due to concerns about rising interest rates and declining affordability. It also states that the decline in sentiment among independent voters exceeded increases in outlook among Republicans and Democrats. It includes quotes from Joanne Hsu, noting that purchasing power dominates consumer views and that sentiment has fallen since just before the start of the U.S. war with Iran.

It further reports that selling prices rose at the fastest rate since Aug. 2022, citing an S&P Global survey of purchasing managers, and includes comments about cost pressures, supply chain bottlenecks, and backlogs prompting companies to raise prices. The article mentions that Fed officials are scheduled to discuss monetary policy on Oct. 27–28, and it provides figures on Brent crude oil prices and inflation expectations for a year from now and for the long run, including quotes from Hsu about above-target inflation and potential entrenchment of elevated expectations.

TITLE: SpaceX Filing Gives Elon Musk the Final Word on Tesla Merger He Says He’s Staying Out Of
CONTENT: The article says Elon Musk recused himself from the SpaceX-Tesla merger talks, and that a SpaceX SEC filing suggests this does not change his influence. It states SpaceX’s October 22 10-Q says any potential combination with Tesla would require further approval by the special committee, the board of directors, and the controlling shareholder, and that Musk controls roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power as the controlling shareholder. The article describes that special committees were formed on October 20 to evaluate a proposed deal estimated to create a combined entity worth around $3.5 trillion, and quotes Musk describing staying out as an “odd kabuki dance” where he cannot be in the conversation, while noting the filing language suggests he will have the last word. It mentions a Reuters report that Musk’s earlier public endorsement created complications for the independent process and the committees’ ability to negotiate at arm’s length. The article also notes critics point to Tesla’s 2016 SolarCity acquisition as a governance precedent and says SpaceX investor disclosures flagged Musk’s overlapping interests as a material risk. It states Tesla shareholders must clear a threshold of 50% of all outstanding shares, not a simpler majority of votes cast, and quotes Musk calling it a “quite a high hurdle.” It adds that Tesla’s annual meeting is December 3.

TITLE: What To Expect From Wednesday’s Federal Reserve Meeting
CONTENT: The article says the Federal Reserve’s policy committee is likely to keep its key interest rate steady when it meets on Wednesday. It notes that economists expect potential future rate increases to address high inflation, but do not expect an immediate second consecutive rate hike after September’s increase. It discusses how higher rates can raise borrowing costs, dampen inflation, and potentially slow the economy, while also affecting the job market. It states markets were pricing in a one-in-ten chance of a quarter-point rate hike, referencing CME Group’s FedWatch tool. It also covers recent discussions by Fed officials about whether to follow up on September’s hike, mentions the Fed’s inflation and employment objectives, and says many experts expect a rate increase in December. The article further describes how a pause in October could give officials more time to assess inflation impacts related to the Iran war’s fuel price effects, and references comments by Fed officials suggesting they did not favor back-to-back rate hikes.

TITLE: American Express (AXP) Reports Q3 Earnings: What Key Metrics Have to Say
CONTENT: American Express (AXP) reported Q3 results for the quarter ended September 2026. Revenue was $20.06 billion, up 8.9% year over year. EPS was $4.68 versus $4.14 in the year-ago quarter. Revenue compared with the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $20.13 billion (surprise of -0.34%). EPS surprise was +4.7%, with consensus EPS estimate of $4.47. The article also lists key company metrics for the quarter, including billed business totals and segments (U.S. Consumer Services, Commercial Services, International Card Services), book value per common share, network volumes, risk-based capital ratios (Basel III common equity tier 1), basic cards-in-force, and various revenue components (total non-interest revenues, net interest income, discount revenue, and net card fees). It concludes with stock performance information over the past month and a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

TITLE: Earnings Preview: Eli Lilly (LLY) Q3 Earnings Expected to Decline
CONTENT: The article states that Wall Street expects Eli Lilly’s (LLY) year-over-year earnings decline on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. It says the stock could move higher if key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report expected October 29, and move lower if they miss. It notes Zacks Consensus Estimate figures: quarterly earnings of $5.38 per share (year-over-year change of -23.4%) and expected revenues of $22.11 billion (up 25.6% from the year-ago quarter). It also describes an estimate revisions trend, including a 0.07% higher consensus EPS estimate over the last 30 days. The article explains an “Earnings ESP” approach used to compare a “Most Accurate Estimate” to the Zacks Consensus Estimate and discusses how positive readings are intended to indicate likely deviation from consensus, with predictive power mentioned for positive ESP readings only. It references that the combination of positive Earnings ESP with certain Zacks Ranks is associated with earnings beats (described as nearly 70% of the time in the article).

TITLE: Intel vs. Qualcomm: A Widening Gap in Revenue
CONTENT: The article contrasts revenue trends of Intel and Qualcomm. It describes Intel’s revenue sources (designing, developing, manufacturing, and marketing CPUs, discrete graphics hardware, and advanced semiconductor components) and notes it closed an upsized $20 billion public offering and initiated targeted workforce reductions in data center and AI groups. It describes Qualcomm’s revenue sources (integrated circuits for mobile communication devices and licensing wireless technology patent rights) and notes it completed an acquisition of a software platform called Modular and announced plans for global workforce reductions. It explains that “revenue” refers to the standardized income-statement revenue line item. It then provides a table of quarterly revenue for Intel and Qualcomm over the last 8 quarters (Q3 2024 through Q2 2026) with amounts and quarter-end dates for each company.

TITLE: F5 to Report Q4 Earnings: What's in the Cards for the Stock?
CONTENT: F5 Inc. (FFIV) is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Oct. 27, after market close. For the quarter, F5 projects non-GAAP EPS of $4.14-$4.26 (midpoint $4.20). The Zacks Consensus Estimate is $4.24, implying a year-over-year decline of 3.2%, and the estimate has remained unchanged for 60 days. The article states that F5 surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters, with an average earnings surprise of 16.09%. F5 projects non-GAAP revenues for the quarter of $870-$890 million, with the Zacks Consensus Estimate at $884.4 million, implying year-over-year growth of 9.2%. The article lists factors to consider, including sustained demand for application delivery and security solutions, demand for systems products (including BIG-IP offerings), and continued traction in subscription-based offerings in the software segment (including BIG-IP and NGINX).

TITLE: Analysts Estimate D.R. Horton (DHI) to Report a Decline in Earnings: What to Look Out for
CONTENT: Wall Street expects D.R. Horton (DHI) to report a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues for the quarter ended September 2026. The earnings report is expected to be released on October 29. The article states that quarterly earnings are expected to be $3.03 per share and revenues are expected to be $9.04 billion. It also notes the consensus EPS estimate has been revised 3.43% lower over the last 30 days. It discusses estimate revisions and describes the Zacks Earnings ESP, which compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate, and notes that a positive Earnings ESP reading is presented as a strong predictor of an earnings beat when combined with certain Zacks Ranks.

TITLE: D.R. Horton (DHI) Cuts 2026 Outlook Following Sales Miss While Undervalued Narrative Holds
CONTENT: D.R. Horton (DHI) cut its fiscal 2026 revenue outlook to US$32.5b to US$33b after third quarter sales missed internal goals, with higher mortgage costs, softer earnings per share, and a 20% cancellation rate pressuring demand. The share price has moved sideways overall, with the stock down 4.63% year-to-date and a 1-year total shareholder return declining 11.10%, while longer-term returns are higher (3-year 42.45% and 5-year 66.80%). The article states D.R. Horton trades below its own intrinsic value estimate and the average analyst target after the guidance reset. It describes a “Most Popular Narrative: 10% Undervalued” with fair value pegged at $154.43 versus a last close of $138.98. It says continued execution on capital efficient land use and operating efficiency, including lot control strategy, external developers, and cycle time improvements, is intended to offset higher lot costs and incentives. It also mentions further reductions in start to close cycle times and focus on lower construction costs per square foot (down 5% year over year in Q3 FY26) as supporting margins, while noting that rising sales incentives and ongoing lot cost inflation could squeeze margins. The article discusses an additional “Another View” about D.R. Horton’s P/E ratio (12.7x), comparing peers and a wider group and referencing a fair ratio estimate of 20.8x.

TITLE: Tyler Technologies (TYL) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
CONTENT: Wall Street expects Tyler Technologies (TYL) to report a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues for the quarter ended September 2026. The article says the stock could move higher if the company’s results top expectations in the upcoming earnings report expected to be released October 28, or move lower if they miss. It states the Zacks consensus calls for quarterly earnings of $3.45 per share and revenues of $651.14 million, with the EPS estimate unchanged over the last 30 days. It also describes the Zacks Earnings ESP approach for predicting earnings surprises and notes that positive Earnings ESP readings are a stronger predictor of an earnings beat when combined with certain Zacks Ranks.

TITLE: Roper Technologies Soars 9.2% on Earnings Beat and Guidance Raise: “Exceeded Our Expectations”
CONTENT: The article says Roper Technologies shares rose 9.2% after a third-quarter adjusted EPS of $5.89 beat the $5.79 consensus and the company raised full-year guidance. It states the stock moved higher while the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 2%, and that full-year adjusted EPS guidance increased to $22.35 to $22.40 from $22.15 to $22.30. The article also reports revenue rose to $2.17 billion with 7% organic growth, adjusted net earnings grew to $586 million, and buybacks contributed to adjusted EPS growth. It discusses forward valuation and mentions expectations for fourth-quarter guidance.

TITLE: Snap-on (NYSE:SNA) misses Q3 2026 revenue estimates, stock drops
CONTENT: Snap-on (NYSE:SNA) fell short of Q3 2026 revenue expectations, with sales flat year on year at $1.28 billion. The article states GAAP profit was $4.64 per share, 5.8% below analysts’ consensus. Visible Q3 2026 highlights include revenue of $1.28 billion versus analyst estimates of $1.33 billion, GAAP EPS of $4.64 versus $4.93 expected, operating margin of 24.7% (down from 26.9% year over year), free cash flow margin of 17.4% (down from 19.9% year over year), and organic revenue rising 2.8% year over year. It also states market capitalization of $19.08 billion and includes a quoted statement from Snap-on’s chairman and chief executive officer describing mixed results and challenges mentioned around diesel prices and franchisees’ inventory levels, along with references to Snap-on Value Creation and the company’s outlook.

TITLE: Snap-On (SNA) Lags Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
CONTENT: Snap-On (SNA) reported quarterly earnings of $4.64 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.91 per share; this compares with $4.71 per share a year ago. The earnings surprise was -5.50%. The company also reported revenues of $1.18 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.59%, compared with $1.19 billion a year ago. The text states Snap-On belongs to the Zacks Tools - Handheld industry, mentions share performance versus the S&P 500, and discusses what investors may watch next, including management commentary and earnings outlook/estimate revisions, concluding that the stock has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) and the current consensus EPS and revenue estimates for the coming quarter and current fiscal year.

TITLE: Graco Sinks 15% as Q3 Miss and Light Q4 Outlook Overshadow “A Solid Quarter”
CONTENT: Graco shares fell 15% after its third-quarter adjusted EPS and revenue missed estimates, and its fourth-quarter revenue outlook came in below consensus. The quarter included 8% sales growth, with acquisitions contributing about half and adjusted operating earnings rising 1% as higher product costs offset price increases. Incoming organic orders rose 7%. Reported third-quarter results included adjusted EPS of $0.81 (below $0.84 consensus) and revenue of $586.4 million (below $590.6 million expected). Fourth-quarter revenue guidance was $610 million to $640 million versus $642.4 million consensus. The article also describes sharp declines for TTM Technologies, Lam Research, and Nokia on the same day, alongside a smaller decline for Snap-on, and compares how outlooks and misses affected their stock moves.

TITLE: Why Snap-on (SNA) shares are falling today
CONTENT: The article says Snap-on (NYSE:SNA) shares fell 5.7% in the morning session after the company reported a decline in net sales and diluted earnings per share for the third quarter of 2026. It states that, per a company press release, net sales slipped 0.6% year over year to $1.18 billion, weighed down by a 2.8% drop in organic sales. It also reports diluted earnings per share declined to $4.64 versus $5.02 in the prior-year period, and that financial services revenue totaled $98.6 million with operating earnings from the division of $68.3 million. The article then says the shares shed some losses and rose to $352.72, down 4.4% from the previous close. It further notes that the stock has had no moves greater than 5% over the last year and that the day’s move indicates the market considers the news meaningful. Finally, it states Snap-on is flat since the beginning of the year, trading at $352.72 per share (15.9% below its 52-week high of $419.31 from July 2026).

TITLE: Bunge (BG) Stock May Be Below Fair Value On Earnings Power
CONTENT: The article discusses Bunge Global’s stock valuation relative to its earnings power. It notes the stock’s recent closing price of US$103.22 and describes shareholders’ multi-year return and the question of how much of that gain is reflected in the earnings multiple. It mentions that factors such as pricing power, cost control, and execution influence an appropriate P/E. It also compares the stock’s roughly 19.6x earnings multiple to the broader food industry average (about 18.6x) and a peer group (closer to 23.2x), characterizing the valuation as a middle ground. The piece states that a fair value framework suggests a higher P/E than the market is assigning and frames the resulting gap as raising questions about whether the market is pricing more risk than the model implies or whether the model is overly generous about business quality. It references the “Simply Wall St Narratives” framing and indicates that the story continues.

TITLE: Will Earnings Beat Change Dow (DOW) Narrative
CONTENT: Dow Inc. reported third quarter 2026 sales of US$11.27b and net income of US$458m, with earnings per share ahead of analyst expectations. The quarter highlights Dow’s pricing actions and cost savings programs contributing to higher earnings, while the firm continues a century long dividend record. The article states that Dow’s “self help” plan in costs and portfolio mix is supported by the reported numbers at an operating level, and identifies near-term factors as execution on US$1.3b of planned self help benefits and a broader US$3b structural program, alongside managing energy and raw material pressures. It describes margin risk from elevated input costs and softer polyethylene demand as an operational overhang even after the earnings beat. It also mentions catalysts and stated targets for US$700m of growth and productivity benefits in 2026 and about US$2b of uplift by 2027, and discusses how better-than-expected earnings could affect debt reduction, funding of projects, and dividend support while tracking interest coverage and litigation risks. It summarizes an analyst framework involving gradual revenue growth, forecasts of 2.3% revenue growth per year over the next three years, and a shift from loss to mid single digit profit margins, including a consensus view of earnings moving from a current loss of US$1.3b to US$2.1b by 2029.

TITLE: How Upcoming Earnings At FirstEnergy (FE) Has Changed Its Investment Story
CONTENT: The article says FirstEnergy is set to report third quarter 2026 results after the market close on 27 October. It states that performance will be shaped by data center and industrial power demand, alongside rising operation, maintenance, and storm restoration costs. It says the earnings release will focus on how effectively FirstEnergy’s Energize365 grid modernization spending translates into returns while offsetting a heavier cost base. The article also discusses how the investment narrative depends on regulated grid and transmission investment matching rising electricity demand from data centers and industrial users, highlighting Energize365 projects improving reliability and capacity while data center load ramps. It mentions that the short-term catalyst is how management ties data center demand and grid upgrades to recoverable rate base growth, and the risk is that higher O&M and storm restoration expenses, combined with heavy capital spending, could pressure free cash flow and customer bill affordability. It states that the capital plan around Energize365 reaffirms $6b earmarked for 2026 and a broader $36b program through 2030. It also describes analyst forecasts, including 4.9% yearly revenue growth for the next three years and higher profitability as regulated projects come through.

TITLE: Learn Why The Bull Case For Illinois Tool Works Stock Could Change Following Quarterly Earnings Preview
CONTENT: The article says Illinois Tool Works is set to report September quarter results, with analyst forecasts of $2.99 per share earnings and $4.26 billion revenue versus the same quarter a year earlier. It highlights Test & Measurement and Electronics and Welding as key segments expected to deliver double digit year-over-year growth and shape the earnings mix. It discusses an investment narrative focused on a steady industrial portfolio and enterprise cost programs, noting the September quarter preview supports the thesis but does not radically change it. It also mentions near-term execution in capex-heavy areas, potential margin pressure risks if price increases lag input costs or if weaker Food Equipment and Specialty Products trends deepen, and management’s emphasis on enterprise initiatives adding about 120 basis points to operating margin in Q1 and Q2 2026. It further notes earlier in 2026 that Welding and Test & Measurement and Electronics posted double digit organic growth, orders ahead of revenue, and that newer products contributed 3% to first half sales. The article includes a narrative tied to revenues of US$18.4b and earnings of US$3.8b by 2029, based on 3.8% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$0.6b from earnings today of roughly US$3.2b.

TITLE: Is Earnings Optimism Altering The Investment Case For Hershey Stock (HSY)?
CONTENT: The article discusses Hershey’s outlook amid expectations for higher earnings and revenue in the September 2026 quarter. It notes that management is leaning on heavier brand spending and product launches across chocolate and snacks. It highlights Dot’s Homestyle Pretzels, acquired in 2021, as a lead salty snack platform and says there are plans to move beyond pretzels into broader snack categories and new mixes by 2027. It frames an “investment narrative” around whether Hershey can convert brand spending and a broader snack portfolio into healthier volumes, discusses operational risks including pricing power and potential capacity or freight issues, and references concerns such as volume decline, U.S. chocolate share loss, and higher leverage. The article states the upcoming September 2026 earnings report expectations of US$2.12 in EPS and US$3.25b in revenue. It also describes Hershey’s investment plans including automation in salty snacks, expanded capacity into 2027, and an innovation slate in chocolate and Dot’s led snacks. It presents a longer-range forecast of US$13.1b in revenue and US$2.1b in earnings by 2029, based on assumptions of 2.6% yearly revenue growth and increased earnings from US$1.5b today.

TITLE: Sherwin Williams (SHW) Faces Higher Earnings Expectations, Is It Trading At An 11% Discount?
CONTENT: The article says Sherwin-Williams (SHW) reaffirmed its income stream by declaring a quarterly dividend of $0.80 per share payable on December 4, 2026, with an ex-dividend and record date of November 13. It states that Wall Street projects higher earnings per share and revenue for the upcoming quarter. It reports the share price reaction as positive, noting SHW is up 2.5% over the last day and has a 5.3% 30-day share price return, with a 1-year total shareholder return of 5.2% and a 3-year total shareholder return of 49.3%. It says the dividend news and the recent share price move place the stock near the middle of its valuation range, about 10% below average analyst targets and roughly 13% below one intrinsic value estimate. It includes a “Most Popular Narrative: 11% Undervalued,” stating Sherwin-Williams is trading at $345.63 with fair value pegged at $389.09, and references a 7.57% discount rate. It mentions a plan to open 80 to 100 net new Sherwin-Williams Paint Stores Group locations each year to reach roughly 6,000 stores, alongside pruning of underperforming sites. It lists potential risks such as raw material inflation tightening margins or weak DIY and construction demand lingering. It also states another valuation view from DCF work, saying the stock trades about 13.2% below an intrinsic value estimate of $398.06, and notes the current P/E is roughly 31x compared with Chemicals industry and peer averages.

TITLE: Meta stock closes out Friday down as AI spending fears continue to rattle markets
CONTENT:
Meta (META) stock closed out Friday down roughly 1%, after Thursday shares plunged 7%. The article says Meta reported better-than-anticipated Q3 revenue, but AI spending fears and renewed concerns about whether AI data center investments will pay off led investors to pull back on AI-related stocks.

It states Meta raised the lower end of its capital expenditure estimate to $135 billion to $145 billion (from $130 billion to $145 billion) and also has $825 billion in various spending commitments tied to cloud capacity arrangements, energy service agreements, and consumer hardware products. It notes analysts were largely bullish due to prospects for its Muse AI agent and models.

The article says CEO Mark Zuckerberg highlighted Muse’s profitability over multiple years, contingent on improving compute efficiency. It reports Q3 revenue of $64 billion (vs. $63.3 billion anticipated) and GAAP earnings per share of $3.83 (vs. $3.56 expected), mentioning legal charges related to a teen mental health settlement.

It also says Meta will issue new nonvoting Class C shares to all Class A stockholders, effectively creating a 2-for-1 stock split, and that a New Mexico judge ordered the company to pay $25 billion related to a consumer-harms case. The article references a proposal (Proposition 40) described as a 5% tax on taxpayers with assets over $1 billion.

TITLE: OpenAI aiming for new $30 billion funding round at a $1.25 trillion valuation
CONTENT: The article says OpenAI is looking to raise a fresh $30 billion funding round that would value the AI lab at $1.25 trillion, and notes it was previously reported to be seeking capital at a $1.5 trillion valuation. It states OpenAI last raised $122 billion in March, valuing the company at $852 billion. It also says rival Anthropic is preparing to file its initial public offering (IPO) ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, with Wall Street anticipating a valuation of as high as $2 trillion. The article mentions the company could reveal its S-1 in the coming days. It describes that OpenAI’s funding discussions are occurring amid declines in AI stocks related to concerns about data center build-out, and mentions CoreWeave in particular. It also says broad declines have affected various sectors, including Meta dropping after raising the lower end of its capital expenditure guidance, and references the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index’s decline over the past five days.

TITLE: SpaceX won't follow Meta's playbook to fund its AI build-out, JPMorgan says
CONTENT: The article says SpaceX (SPCX) would not be expected to surprise investors by issuing a new class of nonvoting stock to fund its AI build-out, and that JPMorgan said SpaceX is not considering raising equity. It quotes a JPMorgan analyst noting capital requirements and that SpaceX indicated available pools of capital on the debt side. It states SpaceX guided to $35 billion to $40 billion in capital expenditures for the fourth quarter, compared with prior quarterly capex figures, and that SpaceX ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt. It also mentions the earnings call and that the company’s CFO did not seem fazed by recent tremors in debt markets amid concerns over neoclouds. It further notes the article’s mention of a reportedly eyeing capital raise of $40 billion with Goldman Sachs and Apollo, and quotes another analyst about calls on capital and SpaceX’s recent announcements and spending ahead.

TITLE: Why Tesla's $5 billion capex cut isn't the warning sign AI stock bears think it is
CONTENT: The article discusses Tesla cutting its 2026 capital expenditures guidance by $5 billion to $20 billion, noting it was lifted by $5 billion to $25 billion three months earlier. It says the quick retrench prompted worries that the cut signals a slowdown in AI demand, and argues Tesla isn’t a hyperscaler, with the cut tied more closely to challenges of making Optimus humanoid robots. It includes a comment from Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives expecting Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon to confirm spending rather than cut, and mentions Big Tech’s market decline on Thursday. The article also references Meta reporting negative free cash flow due to AI spending, issuing a new tranche of stock for its AI build-out, and mentions crude oil rising above $112 a barrel. It concludes that Tesla isn’t blamed, citing that the company cut its full-year capex guide, spent below expectations, turned an expected cash outflow into positive free cash flow, and that related business indicators moved the right way.

TITLE: Big Tech's capex spending looks different this year as Meta and Tesla save for later
CONTENT: The article discusses how “Big Tech” capital expenditures (capex) related to AI spending are being timed differently, focusing on Meta, Tesla, and SpaceX. It says investors are asking when returns will come from AI investments and that spending discipline can be rewarded in high-rate environments. It notes that Meta and Tesla moved costs to a different point on the timeline and mentions longer-term spending plans, including off-balance-sheet plans of $825 billion for Meta and a $100 billion chip plant estimate for Tesla. It also references a report that Meta’s credit risk and bonds were affected after the company stated it would spend about $825 billion in the future. For Tesla, it cites Elon Musk saying the chip plant built with SpaceX will require tens of billions in equipment through early 2028 and likely more than $100 billion over the long term. The article further states that these expenses are not yet on balance sheets and are described as hopes for future growth, contrasting this with Apple’s position and Wall Street’s preferences for a stable hardware business amid AI volatility. It concludes by saying Wall Street can interpret changes to AI investment either as disciplined finance or as a slowdown in AI ambitions.

TITLE: How Elon Musk went from Tesla CEO to the 'most powerful civilian, non-governmental actor in history'
CONTENT: The article discusses Elon Musk’s influence through his companies, particularly Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX), and how his growing business portfolio has expanded his impact beyond corporate leadership into areas tied to national security, international relations, and the global economy. It quotes sources describing Musk as potentially the most powerful civilian non-governmental actor in history and notes that restrictions on SpaceX satellite communications services disrupted Ukraine’s military operations, with conflicting accounts about who ordered the restrictions. It also states that SpaceX is responsible for about 90% of all mass sent into orbit off Earth and describes Starshield’s Pentagon customer role and Starlink use by countries for national communications including emergency services. The text includes quotations characterizing the ability to turn communications on or off as an extraordinary power.

TITLE: SpaceX reportedly wants to lease space on 80,000 cell towers in a bid to challenge Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile
CONTENT: The article says Elon Musk’s SpaceX (SPCX) may be close to “sending another message” to telecom companies and is reportedly looking to lease space on 80,000 cell sites across the US. It states SpaceX is reportedly in talks with Crown Castle and American Tower. The article includes a quoted comment from Bernstein analyst Laurent Yoon about committing to spectrum and macro sites. It also says AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile stock were sharply lower in morning trading, and references SpaceX’s acquisition of a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio earlier in the month. It describes concerns that Starlink could disrupt legacy wireless operators as Starlink transitions toward direct mobile competition, and notes the article’s discussion of SpaceX laying groundwork for a standalone cellular network. Additional quotes from Yoon discuss investor perceptions of Starlink broadband as a threat and “Starlink Mobile” as a longer-term question.

TITLE: SpaceX stock slides as tech trade tumbles
CONTENT: The article says SpaceX (SPCX) shares fell on Thursday, reversing Wednesday’s post-earnings gain. It notes the stock jumped 7.8% on Wednesday after upbeat Q3 results and AI commentary. It states the stock is down 9% alongside broader tech weakness after Meta (META) earnings and additional war-related headlines. It reports SpaceX guided fourth-quarter capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion (from $19.6 billion in Q3) as more compute capacity comes online, and ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt. It quotes an analyst noting large calls on capital ahead and a SpaceX CFO statement about being investment grade and having available debt capital pools. The article also mentions merger discussions involving SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA), including special committees of independent directors and the claim that Musk is recused as a conflicted party, along with Reuters/Bloomberg-referenced reporting about the process and timing. It adds that some banks are more bullish on SpaceX’s prospects, including JPMorgan, BofA, and Barclays comments about targets and a potential shareholder vote venue.

TITLE: Elon Musk says Tesla's Optimus robot needs to learn like a toddler
CONTENT: The article says Tesla CEO Elon Musk compared getting Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robot to human learning, describing bootstrapping through self-play and likening early development to how a toddler learns. It discusses the impact of recent reminders on Wall Street’s medium-term sales estimates for Optimus and mentions Tesla pulling back its planned full-year capital expenditures from $25 billion to $20 billion. It quotes Musk from a late Wednesday earnings call about needing Optimus to play at scale for real-world task performance. The article also states that Tesla ended production of the Model S and Model X at its Fremont, California factory to make room for Optimus robot production, and provides details about Optimus V3 (height, weight, and chips/power source) plus production start and the number of units operating. It includes an analyst quote about expectations for reaching a 1 million unit weekly run-rate and notes timing for early applications and later household use, as well as comments about what the bottlenecks are and Optimus’s potential impact on estimates.

TITLE: The simple reason JPMorgan thinks SpaceX will triple: It's going after a $28 trillion market
CONTENT: The article says SpaceX (SPCX) has gained about 10% on Wednesday after reporting earnings as a public company, including profitability and AI revenue, and has received stock upgrades. It highlights a JPMorgan bullish view, noting analyst Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target to $500 from $240, implying over 200% upside from Wednesday’s price. The article attributes the outlook to the idea that SpaceX is well positioned to go after a combined anticipated total addressable market of $28T+. It also describes SpaceX’s expansion beyond rockets and satellites into telecommunications and AI-related and chip-to-data-center efforts, and discusses potential added markets such as robotaxi and robotics. The article mentions special committees from SpaceX and Tesla to explore a tie-up, and says Musk projected SpaceX’s annual recurring revenue by end of 2027 between $500 billion and $1 trillion.

TITLE: SpaceX stock soars to its best day in 2 months while space peers climb out of a 26% hole
CONTENT: The article says SpaceX (SPCX) opened with its biggest jump since its June debut and is on pace for its best day in two months, while space peers are also rising after earlier declines. It states SpaceX gapped higher after its third-quarter revenue and profit topped Wall Street estimates, and that the company’s AI business now accounts for nearly half of its sales. It also mentions that CEO Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA) formed committees to study a merger. The article compares October performance for SpaceX versus a typical newer space stock and notes that legacy defense names like Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Northrop Grumman (NOC) mostly gained. It describes early-trading movers among newer space stocks and includes references to commentary about SpaceX’s planned capital expenditures and its backlog. It discusses price levels, including support above $140, a ceiling near $172, potential resistance toward the June highs around $210, and a share unlock expected on Thursday. It concludes by stating that readers should watch whether SpaceX holds its gap into the close and whether it stays above $150 through the Thursday unlock.

TITLE: Anthropic to publicly file for IPO as early as Friday, sources say
CONTENT: Anthropic is set to publicly file its S-1 investor prospectus as soon as Friday, according to three people familiar with the plans. The article says the move would be a crucial next step toward a potential IPO and may help test investor appetite. It notes Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft IPO registration statement to the SEC in June and that SEC rules require materials to be made available 15 calendar days before a formal investor roadshow. The article also mentions expected procedural timing toward a potential November listing, and that a public filing would provide regular investors with financial details and risks. It discusses Anthropic’s spending on AI infrastructure, including working with Google and Amazon and renting GPU capacity from SpaceX’s data center. It references revenue and net loss figures reported by other outlets and mentions that investors have become more concerned about the industry’s spending. The article also says other companies’ IPO plans and market events this year have become more challenging.

TITLE: Tech stocks lead market higher as SpaceX shares surge: AlphaCheck
CONTENT: Tech stocks led the market higher. SpaceX (SPCX) shares rose after better-than-expected results, sparking renewed optimism over the AI trade. Tesla (TSLA) stock rose after its CEO hinted at a potential merger between Tesla and SpaceX. Tesla and Meta (META) were both set to report earnings after the closing bell. AI semiconductor companies Nvidia (NVDA) and AMD (AMD) rose, along with memory makers Micron (MU) and SK Hynix (SKHY). Supermicro (SMCI) surged 13% after lifting its fiscal first quarter revenue forecast ahead of its quarterly results next month. Energy stocks (XLE) retreated as Brent crude futures (BZ=F) fell to $108 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate futures (CL=F) hovered near $97 per barrel. Other notable stocks mentioned included Dell (DELL), AT&T (T), and Abbott Laboratories (ABT).

TITLE: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says data center builders have to be 'good neighbors'
CONTENT:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said data center builders need to partner with local communities and act as “good neighbors” by reaching out before starting construction. He discussed the idea of extending to the local community, sharing what the project will bring, and tailoring benefits to community needs.

The article says data center construction has faced opposition in parts of the US, including bans and moratoriums, and mentions New York’s statewide one-year moratorium and Texas pausing aspects of grid connections for new data centers. It also describes political debate and residents’ complaints related to noise, water usage, and electricity costs.

The article states that some companies, including Microsoft and Amazon, have taken steps to win over municipalities, including dropping controversial nondisclosure agreements (NDAs). Huang is quoted discussing actions such as contributing to communities, building facilities like community centers, improving schools, and supporting lower taxes. He also added that companies should be “good visitors” and “good guests,” and stop by to see how they can be helpful before going into a community.

TITLE: Supermicro stock jumps as server maker lifts revenue forecast
CONTENT: Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock jumped as much as 12% on Wednesday, while peers Dell Technologies (DELL) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) gained 5% and 4%, respectively. The article says the AI server maker raised its fiscal first quarter revenue forecast by $4 billion, and now expects revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 30, up from its previous forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. It also says the company raised its gross margin forecast to 12% to 12.5% from a previous outlook of 10.4% to 10.8%, citing a more favorable customer and product mix. The article states that Supermicro will present its complete Q1 fiscal year 2027 financial results on Nov. 3.

TITLE: People are now recognizing Nvidia's compute has a great deal of residual value,' CEO Jensen Huang tells Deirdre Bosa
CONTENT: In an interview, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Wall Street is recognizing the usefulness of using Nvidia hardware as collateral to finance data center expansion. He said Nvidia processors have long-term value that can backstop debt tied to constructing data centers. Huang discussed Nvidia’s ability to use its GPU hardware as a financial instrument, and referenced Nvidia’s agreement in August to create a $500 billion funding pool with six financial institutions. He also said Nvidia’s computing systems are productive for a long time due to widespread use and software upgradability, and described how customer demand for older architectures illustrates longer asset lifecycles. He said the compute is productive, fungible, and durable, and could allow underwriting loans against the asset itself.

TITLE: Musk backs SpaceX-Tesla merger idea as both boards form special committees
CONTENT: The article says Elon Musk stated on SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call that merging SpaceX with Tesla would be a good idea. It also reports that, according to Musk, both SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss the idea and that those committees consist of independent directors. The article mentions that SpaceX stock rose in premarket trading after its Q3 earnings release and that merger speculation drew attention. It further notes discussion of shareholder actions and timing related to Tesla’s annual general meeting, and includes details cited from a Barclays analyst about expectations for a potential deal and how merger timing could affect approval. It also references Musk’s ownership stakes in Tesla and SpaceX and notes a view that SpaceX could be the buyer in an all-stock deal.

TITLE: Nvidia reveals plans for 'an AI factory in a shipping container' to build data centers in weeks, not months
CONTENT: Nvidia says it wants to reduce the time it takes customers to start generating revenue from its AI systems. At its GTC event in Berlin, the company unveiled DSX POD, described as a reference design for an AI data center in a shipping-container-sized box. The article says traditional data center construction can take months to years and that delays increase expenses because revenue generation starts when AI systems begin processing tokens. DSX POD is presented as a faster, modular approach intended to reduce deployment time from six months to 14 days. The article states DSX PODs are meant to arrive on site and be ready to plug into existing power, cooling, and networking infrastructure, and that they are not intended to replace traditional data centers but to enable running AI applications before full facilities are ready. Nvidia also states DSX POD supports liquid cooling and can save up to 54 million liters of water per day versus a standard data center. The article notes Nvidia plans to deliver DSX POD with partners including Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, Dell Technologies, Foxconn, and others starting in early 2027, and suggests faster deployment may help address AI infrastructure bottlenecks such as power and chip sales.

TITLE: Meta and Google are about to have a consumer AI showdown
CONTENT: The article says Meta and Google are positioned for a consumer AI showdown, framing it as a fight to control the next popular tech platform for widely adopted digital assistants. It describes Meta’s Muse as a recently launched AI agent and notes early download and praise. It contrasts how Meta’s users rely on the company differently than users rely on Google and Apple, and discusses that more cautious users might wait for early issues to be resolved. It includes commentary from analysts about Google’s positioning in the AI era and mentions potential catalysts related to a competitive agent and Gemini. The article also discusses tensions between the companies’ legacy businesses and how their digital advertising dominance relates to their AI ambitions.

TITLE: Meta Q3 earnings to test Wall Street's stomach for AI spending
CONTENT: Meta will report its third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. The article states that, for the third quarter, Meta is expected to post earnings per share of $3.56 on revenue of $63.3 billion, based on Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates, compared with $1.05 earnings per share and $51.2 billion revenue in Q3 last year. It also says capital expenditures are projected to increase 117% year over year to $41 billion, and that the Reality Labs segment is expected to have an operating loss of $5.2 billion. The article discusses AI investors’ concerns related to CoreWeave’s debt load and references a Gartner report about AI revenue infrastructure spending and potential write-down risk. It notes Meta’s stock performance over the last year and mentions recent developments such as Muse AI agent reaching 10 million downloads 40 days after its US launch, the debut of Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full AI models, and Meta stock being little changed during premarket hours ahead of earnings. The article also mentions CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta Connect hardware announcements, and includes a quote from a BofA Global Research analyst about Meta’s AI execution and risk of AI disruption. It further references premarket and after-hours stock figures shown on the page.

TITLE: Chip stocks shrug off a scary morning, but history says the shakeout isn't over
CONTENT: The article says chip stocks fell sharply at the open but were leading a comeback by midmorning. It reports that the PHLX Semiconductor Index (^SOX) dropped to its lowest level since early August, then rebounded to be higher on the day and back above Friday’s close. It states that roughly 3 of every 4 stocks in a 60-stock Yahoo Finance chip basket turned green, listing AMD, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), Intel (INTC), and Micron (MU) as examples, and says GlobalFoundries (GFS) tops the list. It notes that chip equipment makers Lam Research (LRCX), KLA (KLAC), and Applied Materials (AMAT) were still in the red, along with Arm (ARM), and that Nvidia (NVDA) was barely keeping up. It argues that a longer track record suggests the downturn’s “real test may still be ahead,” citing Yahoo Finance calculations about past losing streaks and typical declines, and says one-day comebacks have been a “coin flip” for chips. It adds that the index was usually higher three months out and includes discussion of support and resistance levels for the index.

TITLE: Meta's Muse AI agent hits 10.9 million downloads as ChatGPT slides 25%
CONTENT: The article says Meta’s Muse AI agent has amassed 10.9 million downloads since its launch on Sept. 8, citing newly released data from Sensor Tower. It states Muse has received more than 10.2 million downloads from the US alone. It contrasts this with Sensor Tower’s estimate that US downloads for OpenAI’s ChatGPT declined by 25% over the prior 30-day period. The article says Sensor Tower estimated Muse reached 2.5 million daily active users (DAUs) for the first time on Oct. 16, and that DAUs increased 15% week over week for the past seven days. It also mentions that Sensor Tower said only 11 other apps reached 10 million US downloads within 40 days, with Meta’s Threads being the most recent app to do so in July 2023. The article includes a Deutsche Bank analyst view that Muse could reach up to 8% of Meta’s revenue by 2030, and on the lower end $2.4 billion in sales by 2030. It concludes by stating Meta is slated to report earnings after the close of trading on Wednesday.

TITLE: Why Tesla bull Cathie Wood thinks the stock is headed to $5,000
CONTENT: Longtime Tesla (TSLA) bull Cathie Wood of Ark Invest is described as setting out bullish expectations for Tesla into 2027. The article says Ark Invest issued a $4,400 base-case price target for Tesla looking out to 2031, with a bull case of $5,000 and a bear case of $3,300. It states that Tesla stock is trading at $366 today. The article attributes Ark’s updated bullish view to assumptions about robotaxis, humanoid robots, and Terrafab. It includes a quoted explanation from Ark estimating Robotaxi’s contribution to Tesla’s enterprise value in 2031 and describing why the model changes from a prior 2024 model. The article also discusses Tesla’s redesigned Roadster unveiling at SpaceX’s rocket test site in McGregor, Texas, describing stunt footage and details such as performance claims, production start timing, and deposits. It further mentions Ark leaving open the possibility of a Tesla/SpaceX merger and quotes Ark’s view on how the two companies could work together, including combined revenue and EBIT estimates by 2031. The article notes that Wood will be a featured speaker at Yahoo Finance’s annual Invest event on Nov. 12 and includes biographical information about the author.

TITLE: SpaceX investors are very focused on one big financial swing factor
CONTENT: The article says the deciding factor for whether SpaceX stock lifts off in 2027 may hinge on compute power the company sells to AI infrastructure builders. It quotes Deutsche Bank analyst Edison Yu, who says the largest forecast swing factor is compute deployment, with management targeting more than 2 GW exiting 4Q26 and 5–10 GW exiting 2027, while the analyst models toward the low end of about 6 GW and expects line of sight into procuring 5–7 GW of power over the next couple of years. Yu is also cited estimating that SpaceX’s neocloud business could bring in $70 billion to $90 billion in sales in 2027, with third quarter neocloud sales modeled at $6 billion versus $2.2 billion in the second quarter and $360 million in the first quarter. The article also notes that SpaceX reports third quarter earnings after the close on Tuesday, and mentions SpaceX stock is down slightly in October and down about 35% from IPO highs. Additional reported items include a statement by Elon Musk about giving one share of SpaceX stock to every kid in America in 2027 and references to Tesla’s flying Roadster using SpaceX thrusting power, along with a quoted comment about potential Tesla–SpaceX merger timing.

TITLE: Meta stock sinks nearly 7% as AI spend pushes free cash flow negative
CONTENT: Meta shares fell nearly 7% on Thursday after the company reported negative free cash flow in its third-quarter earnings and raised the floor of its expected full-year capital expenditures. The five-year credit default swap spread for Meta reached all-time highs. Meta said it expects full-year capex to range from $135 billion to $145 billion, with the bottom of the range raised from a previous $130 billion. Free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion during the quarter. The company also announced it would create a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock. Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.60 billion, up 26% from a year earlier, and earnings per share of $3.83, though the article says it wasn’t clear if the number was directly comparable to the $5.75 per share Wall Street expected.

TITLE: Comcast beats earnings expectations as media revenue offsets weakness in connectivity
CONTENT: Comcast topped analyst earnings expectations for the third quarter, helped by strength in its media unit. The Peacock streaming service reported a quarterly profit for the second consecutive quarter and maintained 48 million paid subscribers. Comcast said media revenue rose 13% year over year to $5.4 billion. The company’s connectivity and platforms sector continued to face pressure, with revenue down 2.7% year over year, and Comcast reported net customer losses in domestic broadband residential and cable customers during the period. The article also discusses Comcast’s plan to spin off its media business into a separate publicly traded company, including comments about timing for completing the transaction.

TITLE: Procter & Gamble earnings beat as sales rise 4%, boosted by laundry and home products
CONTENT: The article says Procter & Gamble reported quarterly earnings and revenue that beat analysts’ expectations, supported by demand for its laundry detergent and home care products. It notes that shares rose more than 5% in morning trading and provides results for the three-month period ended Sept. 30 versus analyst expectations (adjusted EPS $2.00 vs. $1.88 expected; revenue $23.3 billion vs. $22.8 billion expected). It states fiscal first-quarter net income attributable to the company was $4.73 billion ($1.97 per share), down from $4.75 billion ($1.95 per share) a year earlier, and that excluding certain items earnings were $2 per share. It reports net sales rose 4% to $23.3 billion and mentions volume growth of 2.4%. The article includes commentary from P&G’s CFO about a bifurcated economy, describes volume performance by divisions (fabric and home care up 4.3%, baby/feminine/family care and beauty up more than 2%, grooming down 0.4%, healthcare down 2.9%), and discusses P&G’s expectations and forecast for fiscal 2027, including an updated all-in sales growth range and the impact of its acquisition of Thorne.

TITLE: Southwest Airlines cuts 2026 profit forecast on higher fuel
CONTENT: Southwest Airlines cut its 2026 profit forecast due to higher fuel prices, making it the third major U.S. airline that month to do so. Southwest expects to earn between $2.60 and $2.85 per share on an adjusted basis in 2026, down from its prior July forecast. The article also summarizes third-quarter results versus Wall Street expectations, including adjusted earnings per share of 66 cents versus 58 cents expected and adjusted revenue of $8.42 billion versus $8.25 billion expected. Southwest forecast fourth-quarter adjusted per-share earnings between 55 cents and 80 cents and expects unit revenue to rise up to 21% year over year, with capacity growth up to 4% year over year. The CEO says demand remains strong despite higher fares. The article states third-quarter net income was $270 million (55 cents per share) versus $54 million (10 cents per share) a year earlier and notes changes to Southwest’s business model, including charging for more seat assignments and adding a bag fee. It also mentions Delta Air Lines and United Airlines cut their profit outlooks earlier that month.

TITLE: Tesla beats on earnings and sales even as auto revenue declines
CONTENT: The article says Tesla reported better-than-expected third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday, even as automotive revenue dropped and the stock slid in extended trading. It provides reported vs. estimated figures: earnings per share of 48 cents adjusted vs. 43 cents estimated, and revenue of $28.05 billion vs. $27.9 billion estimated. It states automotive revenue fell 3% year over year to $20.56 billion, energy revenue fell 16% to $2.88 billion, and services and other revenue rose 33% to $4.61 billion. It notes net income attributable to common shareholders fell 29% to $787 million (22 cents per share) from $1.11 billion (32 cents per share) a year earlier, and attributes the profitability drop to increased spending on Optimus humanoid robots and other AI initiatives, along with higher capital expenditures and a decline in free cash flow. It also discusses growth in FSD subscriptions, plans to provide some customer cars access to forthcoming FSD (Unsupervised) systems, Tesla testing Cybercab, and statements about a driverless Robotaxi fleet. The article includes additional commentary about Tesla’s markets and references to vehicle deliveries earlier in the month.

TITLE: Meta reports third-quarter revenue beat and issues strong guidance
CONTENT: CNBC’s live coverage says Meta reported better-than-expected third-quarter revenue and issued strong guidance for the current period. The stock rose about 2.5% in extended trading. The page lists third-quarter figures including earnings per share of $3.83 and revenue of $64.60 billion versus $63.37 billion, and notes revenue jumped 26% from a year ago. It also states Meta expects fourth-quarter revenue between $73 billion and $76 billion (or $74.5 billion at the midpoint), and includes various additional live-update items covering other aspects of Meta’s earnings and related commentary (e.g., guidance and other metrics discussed in the updates).

TITLE: Moody’s holds steady on France’s credit rating as country grapples with turmoil and higher yields
CONTENT: Moody’s maintained France’s credit rating at Aa3 and kept a negative outlook. The negative outlook was attributed to increased risk that fragmentation in France’s political landscape will impair the functioning of the country’s legislative institutions. The article also says Moody’s noted that political instability and social tensions could hamper the French government’s ability to address challenges including an elevated fiscal deficit, a rising debt burden, and higher borrowing costs, potentially weakening key sovereign credit metrics faster than expected. It states Moody’s said it could return the outlook to stable if institutions narrow the deficit. The article notes investors were anticipating the decision amid civil unrest and higher bond yields, including that France’s 10-year bond yield surpassed 5% for the first time since 2002 and that the spread against German bunds is at a 15-year peak. It also mentions France’s deficit-to-GDP ratio is roughly 5.5%, cites a forecast related to France’s debt-to-GDP ratio expected to reach 121.7% in 2027, and says the country faces more than $1 trillion of debt maturing by 2030.

TITLE: Netflix posts third-quarter earnings beat, but shares fall on advertising and revenue guidance
CONTENT: Netflix reported third-quarter results for the period ended Sept. 30. Earnings per share were 87 cents versus 82 cents estimated, and revenue was $12.87 billion versus $12.87 billion estimated. The company said its revenue was almost 12% higher year over year, boosted by growth in membership and increases in subscription prices effective in March. Net income was $3.66 billion, or 87 cents per share, compared with $2.55 billion, or 59 cents per share, the prior year period. Netflix expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise more than 11% to $13.44 billion, and narrowed its 2026 full-year revenue forecast to $51.1 billion. The article also discusses investor focus on engagement and advertising metrics, recent organizational changes, and the company’s discussion in its shareholder letter regarding investor concern about view hours growth. It notes Netflix’s expectations for ad revenue guidance for 2026 and mentions plans described for accelerating growth via entertainment value, technology, and monetization.

TITLE: Musk says Tesla and SpaceX formed special committees to discuss merger: Live updates
CONTENT: CNBC’s live coverage discusses SpaceX’s 2026 third-quarter earnings. It reports that SpaceX shares climbed about 8% in extended trading after the company reported 161% revenue growth for the third quarter, with its artificial intelligence business growing ninefold. On the earnings call, CEO Elon Musk said a merger with Tesla would be a “good idea,” and that the boards of both companies have formed special committees to discuss a tie-up. The coverage includes SpaceX’s results versus LSEG consensus estimates, including revenue of $14.58 billion versus $12.72 billion expected and adjusted earnings per share of 45 cents versus 13 cents expected. It also states SpaceX reported operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion, compared with a net loss of $1.05 billion a year earlier. The article notes CFO Bret Johnsen’s forecast for first-quarter 2027 revenue and discusses revenue by segment, including Starlink connectivity subscriber growth to 13.6 million and AI revenue growth to $7.56 billion. It also mentions SpaceX’s launch business revenue, unit operating income and profit figures, and additional items raised during the call (including plans involving chip production, and Starship milestones).

TITLE: General Motors beats Wall Street’s Q3 earnings expectations, narrows full-year guidance
CONTENT: The article says General Motors beat Wall Street’s third-quarter earnings expectations, narrowed its 2026 full-year guidance, and raised its free cash flow expectations. It also reports GM announced a new multiyear $20 billion stock buyback after completing a prior $6 billion share repurchase program, and that GM did not disclose a specific timeframe for the repurchase. The piece notes GM stock fell nearly 7% during trading Tuesday because the company’s outlook missed Wall Street’s expectations. It provides reported third-quarter adjusted earnings per share and revenue figures versus LSEG estimates, describes the ranges included in GM’s new guidance (including adjusted EBIT and adjusted automotive free cash flow), and discusses commodity inflation and tariff cost expectations. It further mentions quarterly net income attributed to stockholders, North American operations’ contribution to adjusted EBIT, and that GM said costs related to the company’s all-electric vehicle pullback were “substantially completed.”

TITLE: Scalpers offer Apple iPhone Duo buyers hundreds extra outside Beijing launch
CONTENT: The article says Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo was launched globally on Friday. It describes scalpers outside the Beijing flagship Apple store in Sanlitun offering to buy newly purchased Duo phones on the spot for hundreds of dollars more. The piece also references that China is the world’s largest market for foldable phones, and includes comments from people waiting in line and trying to purchase the device, along with additional context about other companies’ foldable launches. It also mentions expectations around Apple Intelligence features and related regulatory timelines and availability in China.

TITLE: With earnings in rearview mirror, SpaceX-Tesla merger chatter takes center stage
CONTENT: The article discusses Elon Musk’s comments on a potential merger between SpaceX and Tesla, including that he said it would be a “good idea” and that special committees have been formed to explore a transaction. It also notes that Tesla’s investor relations said executives would not be addressing the matter before an earnings call. The piece describes market reaction around Tesla and SpaceX shares, references analyst perspectives on merger motivation and control, and outlines points about voting power for SpaceX and Tesla based on their share structures and filings. It further mentions that regulatory and cross-border issues could be significant, with comments attributed to experts and an analyst. The article also references other recent company activities involving Musk’s businesses and prior remarks about the possibility of a merger. In addition, it includes stock ticker display text for TSLA and lists an “Elon Musk” quote and other attributed quotations visible in the body text.

TITLE: On the ground at Nvidia’s AI showpiece: Jensen-mania, robot ducks and neocloud distress
CONTENT: The article reports from Nvidia’s GTC in Berlin, describing it as the final event of a week-and-a-half European tour by CEO Jensen Huang. It says Huang met with world leaders, announced new products, and discussed taking part in conversations centered on “neocloud distress,” small data centers, and capital availability. It includes Huang’s comments about demand for capital and neocloud demand. The article also discusses a selloff among public neocloud stocks, concerns among conference attendees about businesses with no credit rating, and Huang’s announcement of a new product designed to bring data center deployments online faster. It further mentions estimates for AI-related capital spending and describes capital as a potential bottleneck, alongside references to smaller data center deals being explored by major compute consumers. It concludes with additional newsletter-related and CNBC site sections not related to the main article narrative.

TITLE: Nvidia’s Huang heads to Kazakhstan for the first time — and he’s not the only one with big plans
CONTENT: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang visited Kazakhstan for the first time, saying the country could become a major AI computing hub serving Europe. The article says Nvidia and investment firm TCV invested in an extension of Higgsfield’s Series B funding round. It also describes Kazakhstan’s AI and digitalization plans, including government statements about AI infrastructure investment and efforts to build AI computing clusters. The article further notes that an initiative called Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz is planned as an AI infrastructure hub, and discusses other international investment plans in Kazakhstan’s digital infrastructure. Finally, it mentions Volkswagen’s expansion into Central Asia through its China operations and references a recent SCO-related event in Kazakhstan focused on artificial intelligence.

TITLE: Meta’s deal to keep Zuckerberg in California adds fuel to wealth tax debate ahead of election
CONTENT: The article says Meta put in place a new stock plan to help offset the burden of higher taxes if a California wealth tax (Proposition 40) passes on Election Day. It describes the filing that disclosed the plan alongside Meta’s third-quarter earnings report and notes that Mark Zuckerberg would be able to sell or transfer up to 20% of newly granted shares for potential tax liability without affecting his majority voting control. The article also discusses that Meta said Zuckerberg committed to remaining in California for eight years, and includes comparisons to other tech executives’ residences and commentary about opposition and support for Proposition 40, along with details about polling and statements attributed to various figures. It further states that Meta and a special committee view Zuckerberg as key to the company’s strategy and stability and that the company created a new class of non-voting Class C common stock to take effect in January.

TITLE: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says neocloud demand is ‘off the charts’ but capital is scarce
CONTENT: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that demand for neoclouds is “off the charts,” but growth is limited by scarce working capital. He said the demand for capital exceeds the availability and that the issue will be solved. Huang discussed power constraints for the AI boom, especially in Europe where electricity prices are higher, and said energy allocation is crucial for companies such as Nebius and Mistral. He said Europe needs more neoclouds and that building infrastructure in Europe is important to create an AI ecosystem there. The article also describes recent selling pressure on neocloud stocks, citing concerns about spending on AI infrastructure and longer-than-expected return on investments, along with investor worries about debt used by CoreWeave. It states Nvidia has been expanding investments in Europe’s AI sector, including commitments of nearly $10 billion and investments in the UK and France.

TITLE: Critical PHP web security flaws spark global alarm as Google, OpenAI and Amazon respond
CONTENT: The article reports on critical PHP web security vulnerabilities known as “PHP2Shell.” It states the flaws could allow remote execution of malicious code on affected servers. Governments worldwide issued urgent warnings, and the U.S. NSA and FBI issued advisories about preparing security updates and potential risks to server file systems, databases, sensitive data, and networks. Amazon says its threat intelligence team detected attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities before public disclosure, though it is unclear how attackers obtained information. The article also describes work by Google (including Wiz and Gemini) and OpenAI, as well as Cloudflare deploying protections via a web application firewall. It notes that the PHP development team released security fixes and urges operators to identify affected versions and apply updates.

TITLE: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
CONTENT: Meta was ordered to pay $25 billion in penalties by a New Mexico court as part of a data privacy case stemming from the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The article says a jury in Santa Fe found Meta liable for misleading state citizens about how it safeguards and collects user data and prevents harmful information on its services. It also states a New Mexico judge wrote in a filing that “Facebook did not conduct the comprehensive investigation that it promised” after the Cambridge Analytica revelations. The filing described an initial amount awarded to the state and that the penalty was ultimately reduced to $25 billion, along with interest terms described by the judge. The article also includes statements from New Mexico’s attorney general and from Meta’s chief legal officer criticizing the penalty and saying the company will appeal. The article further describes prior related settlements and the procedural history of the case, including earlier lawsuits and trial outcomes mentioned in the text.

TITLE: Intel hits construction milestone at Ohio chip fab that’s at least 5 years behind schedule
CONTENT: Intel announced Oct. 21, 2026 that crews installed the first major structural truss at its new chip fabrication plant in New Albany, Ohio. The Ohio project is described as being at least five years behind schedule. The article says Intel still needs customers to make the investment pay off. It references September reports that SK Hynix could team up with Intel in Ohio, but states neither company confirmed plans. The Ohio factory timeline is described as having been expected to start delivering chips in 2025, then pushed back to finish construction in 2030, with a second Ohio fab planned for completion in 2031. The article also discusses Intel’s Arizona fab, stating that by late 2025 it was in high-volume production at its 18A chip node and that operations at the next Arizona fab are expected by the end of 2028. The article mentions that Intel has yet to land a major external customer for its Arizona 18A chips and uses them to make its own processors. It also notes rising demand for advanced chips tied to AI and competition for space at major foundries.
